records.text: Owens cited a New York Times report as saying the Stern Gang tried to assassinate President Harry S. Truman by letter bomb in 1947.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It reads, letter bombs mailed to Truman. And it tells us that the so-called stern gang of the Zionist terrorists tried to assassinate President Truman by letter bomb in 1947, according to a new biography written by Mr.

verification.notes: The cited New York Times article exists under the headline Letter-Bombs Mailed to Truman in 1947 and reported Margaret Truman's biography as saying Stern Gang letter bombs were sent to the White House to kill President Truman. Contemporary reporting independently documents the Stern Gang's 1947 letter-bomb campaign, though the White House attribution chiefly derives from the biography and mail-room account.

sources.title: Letter-Bombs Mailed to Truman in 1947
sources.relevance: The New York Times report cited by Owens, based on Margaret Truman's biography.

sources.title: Stern Gang Claims Responsibility For Letter-Bombs
sources.relevance: Contemporary June 1947 account of the Stern Gang claiming responsibility for the letter-bomb campaign.

records.text: Owens cited Wikipedia as saying Canaanism was founded in 1939, peaked among Jews in Mandatory Palestine during the 1940s, and included former Irgun or Lehi members.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It reads, it tells you that Irgun was a Jewish Canaanite. Canaanism was a cultural and ideological movement founded in 1939, reaching its peak among the Jews of mandatory Palestine during the 1940s. It had a significant effect on the course of Israeli art, literature and spiritual and political thought. Its adherents were called Canaanites. OK, and then it tells you.

verification.notes: The current Canaanism article contains all three cited details: founding in 1939, peak influence among Jews in Mandatory Palestine in the 1940s, and that most members were former Irgun or Lehi members. This verifies the citation claim, not every broader characterization made around it.

sources.title: Canaanism
sources.relevance: The cited Wikipedia entry contains the dates and former Irgun/Lehi membership language summarized in the statement.
